features.name: Hanbit Nuclear Power Plant reactor building (R1)

provenance.note: Reactor containment building at the Hanbit (Yonggwang) Nuclear Power Plant, identified in OSM by power=generator, generator:source=nuclear. Assignment to reactor number R1 (of 6, numbered geographically southwest to northeast) is inferred from which numbering direction gives the best nonlinear least-squares fit of the RENO proposal's own per-reactor near/far detector distances (arXiv:1003.1391 Table 1.2) against these six OSM building positions (residuals under 6 m on distances of 300-1560 m for this SW-to-NE numbering, versus hundreds of metres for the reverse numbering or any other reactor-to-building permutation); see geometry:reno-near-detector method and the worklog. The table itself does not give reactor coordinates, only the SW-NE physical order of the six buildings is used, not a claim about which specific numbered unit (Hanbit's own operator-assigned Unit 1-6 numbering) each is.

features.name: Hanbit Nuclear Power Plant campus boundary

provenance.note: OSM's power=plant boundary polygon for the Hanbit Nuclear Power Plant campus, drawn for surface context only; it is not a claim about either RENO detector hall (both are underground, offset from this boundary -- see geometry:reno-near-detector and geometry:reno-far-detector).

features.method: Nonlinear least-squares multilateration (scipy.optimize.least_squares on raw Euclidean centre-to-centre distance residuals, local equirectangular projection) of this detector hall's position from the six Hanbit reactor-core buildings (geometry:hanbit-core-r1..r6; accuracy_m 8 each), using the per-reactor near/far distances published in the RENO proposal (arXiv:1003.1391, Table 1.2, 'Distances of the reactor cores from the near and far detectors'). Of all 6! possible assignments of the table's R1-R6 labels to the six OSM buildings (and the reflection of the whole line), only the natural southwest-to-northeast geographic numbering converges to a good fit (residual root-mean-square 3-5 m on baselines of 300-1560 m, i.e. well under 2%); every other assignment leaves a residual of hundreds of metres, so this numbering (not independently sourced -- the proposal gives no reactor coordinates) is adopted on that self-consistency alone. accuracy_m is set above the fit residual to also cover the OSM buildings' own ~8 m footprint accuracy and this table being the experiment's 2010 design/proposal figure rather than an as-built survey (the collaboration's own later papers confirm the same overall geometry only as flux-weighted averages: 294 m / 1383 m from the array centre, arXiv:1204.0626).
